title: Angle Bisector Existence Theorem
statement: Every nonstraight angle has exactly one interior ray that divides it into two congruent angles.
theoremLatex: \begin{gathered}\text{Given }\angle ABC\text{ is nonstraight} \\ \text{Then there is exactly one interior ray }\overrightarrow{BD}\text{ satisfies }\angle ABD\cong\angle DBC\end{gathered}
summary: Each nonstraight angle has one and only one ray that splits its opening into two equal angle sizes.
proofIdea: Put the two sides of the angle on one protractor scale, at 0° and θ°. The unique ray at θ / 2 lies inside the angle and makes both parts θ / 2°. Any ray that made equal parts would have to have that same coordinate, so the bisector is unique.
explorationPrompt: Change the opening and move the interior ray. Find the one position where the two angle sizes match, then compare any other position with it.

proofSteps.title: Set one degree scale
proofSteps.detail: For a nonstraight angle ∠ABC, choose a Protractor coordinate system with ray BA at 0° and ray BC at θ°, where 0 < θ < 180.

proofSteps.title: Choose the halfway ray
proofSteps.detail: The Protractor Axiom gives a unique ray BD at coordinate θ / 2. Since 0 < θ / 2 < θ, the order of the coordinates places BD inside ∠ABC.

proofSteps.title: Show that the parts are congruent
proofSteps.detail: The two parts have sizes ∠ABD = θ / 2 and ∠DBC = θ − θ / 2 = θ / 2. Angle Addition confirms that these adjacent parts make the whole angle, so ∠ABD ≅ ∠DBC.

proofSteps.title: Show that no other bisector exists
proofSteps.detail: Any interior ray that divides ∠ABC into two congruent angles makes two equal sizes whose sum is θ°. Each size must therefore be θ / 2. Protractor uniqueness says that ray is BD.
